identification.summary: Storm-1152 is the Microsoft name for a Vietnam-based cybercrime-as-a-service (CaaS) provider that created and sold fraudulent Microsoft accounts and sold CAPTCHA-bypass services; Microsoft estimated it created about 750 million fraudulent accounts for sale [S1][S2]. Microsoft says the accounts served as a gateway to downstream crime such as mass phishing, identity theft, fraud and DDoS [S2].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft analyst Matthew Mesa began tracking the activity in February 2023 [S1]. Arkose Labs is reported to have tracked the group since August 2021 [S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Storm-1152 (financially motivated) [S7]. The existing record lists country 'FIN', which is not supported by any source reviewed; sources place the operators in Vietnam [S1][S2]. Websites and brands named by sources: Hotmailbox[.]me, 1stCAPTCHA, AnyCAPTCHA, NoneCAPTCHA (December 2023) and RockCAPTCHA (2024) [S3][S1][S4]. Storm-1152 is a service provider, not an intrusion set; customers are tracked as separate clusters (Octo Tempest, Storm-0252, Storm-0455) and their activity must not be merged into this profile [S2].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor is asserted in the sources reviewed. Microsoft describes a financially motivated criminal enterprise run by three Vietnam-based individuals [S2][S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft names Duong Dinh Tu, Linh Van Nguyen (also rendered Nguyen Van Linh) and Tai Van Nguyen as the operators and filed civil action against them; these are civil allegations, not criminal convictions [S2][S1][S3]. A criminal referral to US law enforcement was mentioned in search-result summaries but not verified against a fetched source.
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Intelligence and Digital Crimes Unit (DCU) investigation with Arkose Labs threat intelligence, resulting in a US District Court (SDNY) order dated 7 December 2023 [S2][S3]. Individuals are said to have operated the sites, written code, produced video tutorials and run chat support [S1].

objectives: Financial gain by selling fraudulent accounts and CAPTCHA-bypass services to other criminal actors [S2][S1]. Payments were reportedly accepted via PayPal and cryptocurrency [S1].

sectors: Technology platforms and online account providers (Microsoft consumer and enterprise services were the largest victim of the bypass services)
Microsoft partners and supply-chain members affected by fraudulent sign-ups
targeting.notes: Microsoft names no end-victim sectors or regions for the service itself; it refers to 'well-known technology platforms' [S1][S2]. Downstream victims depend on the customer actors that bought accounts. US-based hosting was seized by court order [S2][S1].

capabilities.summary: Storm-1152 ran bots that harvested CAPTCHA tokens in bulk and sold them before expiration, used harvested tokens to create fraudulent Microsoft accounts for resale, and operated CAPTCHA-solving services (1stCAPTCHA, AnyCAPTCHA, NoneCAPTCHA, later RockCAPTCHA) marketed to defeat any CAPTCHA, including Arkose Labs' [S1][S3][S4]. Microsoft reports the group pivoted from bypass tools to account resale after detection, used AI to generate human-like signatures to evade detection, recruited AI engineers in Vietnam and China, and onboarded customers with video tutorials and chat support [S1]. Microsoft said it blocked or suspended over 60% of sign-ups it identified as abusive [S1].

campaigns.name: Arkose Labs begins tracking
campaigns.summary: Arkose Labs is reported to have been tracking the group from August 2021.

campaigns.name: Microsoft profile created
campaigns.summary: Microsoft analyst Matthew Mesa noticed mass phishing using Outlook accounts and created the Storm-1152 profile.

campaigns.name: Fraudulent sign-up surge
campaigns.summary: A major Microsoft customer suffered outages tied to fraudulent sign-ups; Microsoft blocked new Outlook and Hotmail sign-ups and engaged the DCU. Sign-up traffic later dropped about 60% after coordinated action with Arkose Labs.

campaigns.name: SDNY seizure order against Hotmailbox.me and CAPTCHA sites
campaigns.summary: On 7 December 2023 Microsoft obtained a Southern District of New York order to seize US-based infrastructure; seized sites included Hotmailbox[.]me, 1stCAPTCHA, AnyCAPTCHA and NoneCAPTCHA. Microsoft announced the action on 13 December and named Octo Tempest (Scattered Spider), Storm-0252 and Storm-0455 as account buyers.

campaigns.name: RockCAPTCHA domain seizure
campaigns.summary: Under a court order dated 23 July 2024 Microsoft took control of rockcaptcha[.]com, a successor service offering to defeat Arkose Labs CAPTCHA. Secondary reporting says the group had resumed on a smaller scale after December 2023.

diamond.adversary: Three Vietnam-based individuals named by Microsoft in civil action; financially motivated CaaS operators [S2][S1].
diamond.capability: CAPTCHA-token harvesting bots, CAPTCHA-solving services, bulk fraudulent account creation, AI-assisted evasion [S1][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Public storefront and support websites (Hotmailbox[.]me, 1stCAPTCHA, AnyCAPTCHA, NoneCAPTCHA, rockcaptcha[.]com), social media promotion accounts, and US-based hosting seized under court order; payments via PayPal and cryptocurrency [S3][S1][S2].
diamond.victim: Microsoft consumer and enterprise account services and other technology platforms; indirect victims of customers such as Octo Tempest [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Criminal service economy supplying other criminal actors; no state direction is cited [S2].
diamond.technology: Account-creation and sign-up systems that rely on CAPTCHA as a human-verification control [S1].

gaps: Primary Microsoft blog (blogs.microsoft.com, 2023-12-13), CyberScoop, and Arkose Labs pages could not be fetched in this environment; facts rely on a fetched Microsoft Security Insider article and search-result summaries [S1][S2][S3].
The SDNY complaint (published on DocumentCloud) was not opened; the specific legal counts and defendant roles are unverified.
Whether a July 2024 filing was a new complaint or a follow-on order in the same case is unclear from reporting [S4].
Current status after 2024, any criminal charges, and the real-world identity or location details beyond 'Vietnam' are not established.
The country code 'FIN' in the existing record is unsupported and likely wrong.
Customer overlap: Octo Tempest, Storm-0252 and Storm-0455 are separate Microsoft clusters; extent of other buyers is unknown [S2].
Volume figures (750 million accounts, 60% reduction) are Microsoft estimates, not independently verified [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Account-registration and identity-verification systems (webmail, cloud sign-up, CAPTCHA) are the relevant terrain; they are commercial, not military. STEP 2: Storm-1152 is an enabler, not a state actor; it lowers the cost for other actors to obtain disposable accounts at scale [S2][S1]. STEP 3: Template is CAPTCHA-token harvesting, bulk account creation, resale, with rapid rebranding and domain changes after takedown [S1][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued commercial resale under new brands supporting phishing and fraud against organizations including DoD-adjacent ones. MDCOA is that a state or advanced criminal actor buys bulk accounts to stage phishing, infrastructure registration or influence activity; this is analytic inference not stated in sources. Candidate indicators: bursts of new webmail accounts contacting an organization, repeated sign-ups sharing CAPTCHA token patterns, and domains matching named services [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: treat bulk-created webmail accounts as a phishing-precursor indicator and share indicators through established threat-sharing channels. (2) Authorities: the disruption was civil litigation by a private company, not a government action; military cyber forces have no apparent role against this actor absent a separate legal basis. (3) Mission assurance: apply email-filtering and reputation controls that do not assume free-webmail senders are legitimate. (4) Coordination: coordinate with DC3, law enforcement and commercial providers such as Microsoft, who hold the takedown knowledge [S2].
